items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: when I had Peewee Russell and George Brunis, Joe Sullivan, Eddie Condon and Dave Tough on drums. A good band.

ctx.x: One is a Benge coronet that he, Eldon Alvin Benge made for me. He was the first trumpet player in the Chicago Symphony Orchestra for quite a few years. And he started, was making trumpets. But he heard me play at a place called the 'Brass Rail' in Chicago when I had Peewee Russell and George Brunis, Joe Sullivan, Eddie Condon and Dave Tough on drums. A good band. And Eldon Alvin Benge who was a marvellous musician, first trumpet player with the Chicago Symphony.

items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: Jimmy was a sweetheart. I loved it. ... Uh, but Jimmy was a doll. I mean, I love Jimmy.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's what I'm in. I mean, after, yeah, that's what I said.

So, uh, Bill Davis' wife run up, and when she found out, she says, oh, my Bill's got to work with Brunus. So, uh, Bobby Hackett was staying at the bar, and we were talking Condon, Pesky, and so Condon says, well, he says, I got to do something I never did in my life. I hate to do it. I got to fire two guys. I think it was Brad Gowns and, uh, Max Kaminsky. So, uh, he says, I got to put Barnum and Bailey in there. So Bobby Hackett says, look, no matter who you're putting in, as long as you do business, he says,…
Bob Wilbur, is he with you?

items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now who is this, 'Brunies' (Brunees?). >> [INTERVIEWEE] George Brunies.
